requirements.requirement: Stop usb-storage module from loading immediately
requirements.summary: Baseline confirmed module not loaded; /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-usb-storage.conf written with blacklist + install /bin/false directives; modprobe usb-storage immediately failed with 'could not insert usb_storage: Invalid argument', directly demonstrating the block is active now.

requirements.requirement: Stop usb-storage module from loading after a reboot
requirements.summary: Initramfs was regenerated (dracut -f --regenerate-all) and confirmed free of usb_storage via lsinitrd. A real reboot was then performed: boot_id transitioned from a70d7f83... to a8628c34..., directly confirming a genuine restart. Post-reboot, the blacklist config file was still present and modprobe usb-storage still failed, directly demonstrating the block survives a reboot rather than relying on configuration alone.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — blocking usb-storage from loading immediately and persisting the block across reboot — are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence. The executor wrote a modprobe.d blacklist/install-false config, verified an immediate modprobe failure, regenerated and confirmed a clean initramfs, then executed a real reboot (verified via boot_id change from a70d7f83... to a8628c34...) and re-verified post-reboot that the module remains blocked. This fulfills the stricter evidentiary bar required for persistence/reboot claims (healthy baseline, disruption, restoration, recovered state all directly observed).
limitations: Lifecycle before_prepare/after_prepare snapshots are identical (prepare disabled), limiting their usefulness for isolating preparer- vs executor-caused state, though this does not affect assessment of executor actions since all state changes were captured in the executor timeline.
The /tmp/reboot.log artifact left behind is minor residue from the reboot mechanism and was not explicitly cleaned up, though it has no functional impact.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all state-changing commands in order: writing the modprobe.d blacklist file (cmd-915e57bdec0a4f6f) directly implements the requirement; the modprobe test attempt (cmd-eafe6b9a7aa640d0) is a read/verification action with an expected failure exit, not a harmful mutation; the dracut initramfs regeneration (cmd-eafe6b9a7aa640d0) is a necessary prerequisite for reboot-time persistence given usb-storage exclusion needed regenerating the image; the reboot itself (cmd-075f23924c594c98) is required to produce the mandated restart evidence. The reboot trigger's stdout redirect created /tmp/reboot.log, a minor, low-risk, expected artifact of the reboot mechanism rather than an unrelated mutation, and it was not cleaned up, but it is trivial residue with no functional or security impact. No unnecessary, broad, or destructive mutations were found; failed-services and package-health checks show no damage after_executor.
